package_info.why_malicious: Hack$#!t is a Phishing-as-a-Service (PhaaS) platform explicitly designed to enable illegal phishing campaigns. It facilitates credential theft by serving phishing pages from secure, legitimate-looking domains, capturing victim credentials, and exfiltrating stolen data via encrypted WebSocket connections. Its core functionality is the automated theft and exfiltration of sensitive user data, making it inherently malicious.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when victim submits credentials on phishing page)
execution_context.file_location: phishing bait page (HTML/JavaScript served to victim)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when the victim submits credentials on the phishing page, the code establishes a WebSocket connection to the attacker's server, encodes the captured username and password in base64, and transmits them over the encrypted channel, resulting in immediate credential exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code captures sensitive user credentials and transmits them to an external, attacker-controlled server using a WebSocket connection, which is atypical for legitimate authentication flows and indicative of credential theft.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate web authentication forms submit credentials via HTTPS POST to trusted endpoints, not through WebSocket connections to third-party domains.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: WebSockets are commonly used for real-time features such as chat or notifications, but are not used for transmitting authentication credentials, especially to untrusted domains.
key_indicators: WebSocket connection to external, non-affiliated domain
Base64 encoding of sensitive credential data
Credential submission bypassing standard HTTPS POST methods
No user notification or legitimate authentication flow

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when the phishing page is loaded, the browser executes a base64-encoded JavaScript payload embedded in a data URI within a <script> tag, which obfuscates the malicious logic and initiates credential capture routines.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Embedding base64-encoded JavaScript in a data URI is a common obfuscation technique used to evade static analysis and conceal malicious code from both users and automated scanners.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate web pages rarely use base64-encoded inline scripts, especially in authentication contexts, as this practice hinders code transparency and maintainability.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Base64-encoded scripts may be used for small widgets or to embed simple functionality, but are not appropriate for handling authentication or sensitive user data.
key_indicators: Use of data URI scheme for script source
Obfuscated code execution in authentication context
Lack of transparency in script content

attack_chain.action: Phishing bait page is served to the victim from a secure (HTTPS) domain with a legitimate-looking TLD.
Base64-encoded JavaScript is loaded and executed in the victim's browser to obfuscate malicious actions.
Victim enters credentials into the phishing form.
attack_chain.leads_to: Credentials are captured by malicious JavaScript.

attack_chain.action: Captured credentials are encoded in base64 and sent via a secure websocket to the attacker's PhaaS platform.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives and stores stolen credentials.

behavioral_signatures: Phishing pages serving or executing base64-encoded JavaScript via data URIs
WebSocket connections initiated from login or credential input pages to untrusted or non-affiliated domains
Credential submission mechanisms that bypass standard HTTPS POST to legitimate authentication endpoints
file_indicators: Inline <script> tags with base64-encoded payloads using data:text/javascript;base64,
Phishing bait pages containing obfuscated or unreadable JavaScript in authentication flows
Phishing pages hosted on recently registered domains or domains with unusual TLDs
network_indicators: WebSocket (wss://) connections to domains not associated with the legitimate service (e.g., wss://hackshit.example.com)
Outbound network traffic containing base64-encoded credential payloads over WebSocket
Connections to known PhaaS infrastructure or domains flagged for phishing activity
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for web pages, especially those with login or credential input forms, that load or execute base64-encoded JavaScript via data URIs. Flag any WebSocket connections initiated from authentication pages to untrusted or non-affiliated domains. Detect credential submissions that do not use standard HTTPS POST methods to known endpoints. Correlate with domain reputation, recent registration data, and known PhaaS infrastructure to identify suspicious hosting environments.
